project_type: Native Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) with a shared pure-Kotlin JVM core module AND a Kotlin/JVM cloud relay server. Working product name: 'Linkup' (device-to-device ecosystem for Android). HYBRID transport: local Wi-Fi direct path + cloud relay so paired devices sync even on different networks / when the phone is remote.
build_system: Gradle 8.14.5 (Kotlin DSL). Multi-module: :core (java-library / Kotlin JVM, unit-testable in sandbox), :relay (Ktor server, Kotlin JVM, runnable+testable in sandbox), and :app (Android application, requires Android SDK not present in sandbox).
test_framework: JUnit4 + kotlin-test for :core (runs on JVM here). Android instrumentation tests documented but not runnable in sandbox.
build_command: Sandbox-feasible: `./gradlew :core:build :relay:build` and tests below (pure JVM). Full app build `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` requires Android SDK (NOT available in sandbox - user runs on their machine with Android Studio).
test_command: `./gradlew :core:test :relay:test` (runnable in sandbox). Android tests require device/emulator.
verification_instructions: In sandbox: run `./gradlew :core:test :relay:test` to verify protocol/pairing/e2e-crypto logic and the relay routing of sealed envelopes between two simulated remote clients. The :app module is validated by structural/code review only because no Android SDK is installed. On-device + relay-deployment verification steps (for the user, in Android Studio) are documented in docs/VERIFICATION.md.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradle/wrapper/*) is generated via `gradle wrapper`. No other generated/snapshot files checked in. build/ and .gradle/ are gitignored.
setup_instructions: Sandbox: Java 25 + Gradle 8.14.5 pre-installed; run `gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.14.5` once to generate the wrapper, then `./gradlew :core:test`. For the user: open the project in Android Studio (Giraffe+), let it install the matching Android SDK + build tools, then Run on a device/emulator (API 26+).
environment_constraints: No Android SDK / emulator / adb in sandbox -> cannot assemble APK or run instrumentation tests here. Network reaches Maven Central and Google Maven so Gradle can resolve JVM deps for :core. Android Gradle Plugin tasks in :app cannot run without the SDK. Strategy: keep all platform-independent logic (wire protocol, message framing, pairing codes, discovery service info model, clipboard payload model, crypto key-agreement helpers that only need JVM crypto) in :core and unit-test it on the JVM; keep Android-only glue in :app for on-device verification.
contribution_requirements: No existing CONTRIBUTING.md (greenfield). New git repo required at publish time. Conventional-commit style for feature commits.
key_patterns: Clean separation: :core (no Android deps) holds domain + protocol + end-to-end-encryption logic (payload sealing/opening, pairing key material); :app depends on :core and provides Android services (NSD discovery, foreground sync service, clipboard access, MediaProjection/screenshot, Compose UI, relay WebSocket client, FCM wake-up); :relay is a Ktor WebSocket server that routes END-TO-END-ENCRYPTED envelopes between paired devices and never sees plaintext. HYBRID transport with graceful fallback: (1) if peers are on the same LAN -> NSD/mDNS discovery + direct encrypted socket (fast, no cloud); (2) otherwise -> both devices stay connected to the relay over WebSocket and exchange the same sealed envelopes, so sync works when the phone is on mobile data / far away. Pairing via short code / QR establishes a shared pairing secret from which per-link symmetric keys are derived; the relay authenticates by pairing/device IDs but cannot decrypt payloads.
directory_structure: /projects/sandbox root holds the Gradle multi-module project. :core = pure Kotlin JVM library (protocol, pairing, e2e-crypto, models) that compiles & tests in-sandbox. :relay = Ktor WebSocket relay server (Kotlin JVM) that routes sealed envelopes between remote devices; runnable and testable in-sandbox. :app = Android application module (manifest, services, Compose UI, LAN + relay transports) requiring the SDK. docs/ holds the multi-phase plan (ARCHITECTURE, ROADMAP, VERIFICATION). .agents/tasks/ holds this plan state.
